summary: Snapshot 2026-11-24, two days before Thanksgiving. Three things are moving this week. (1) The holiday table is at its peak and should be served only through Shorts that link to the Thanksgiving long video. TODAY, Yahoo, NewsNation, Atlanta Magazine and Prevention all covered it on 11-22 and 11-23, and the window closes 11-27. Prevention's 'Should you skip your GLP-1 during the holidays?' is dosing-adjacent. Don't answer it. Redirect it to 'ask your prescriber'. (2) 'Why weight loss varies' is rising fast. Coverage is spreading from a ScienceDaily release (11-18) to SciTechDaily (11-21), then Qazinform, then UNILAD (11-23). This is the best fresh hook for a tirzepatide 'not working?' or 'after 6 months' long video. The University of Alberta source is a review plus an observational metabolic-adaptation study, so call it 'may help explain', never 'causes'. (3) A second wave of NAION eye-warning stories: 'FDA requires semaglutide labels…' (11-23), plus lawsuit stories. The label-change format is proven, but steer away from the lawsuit framing. Newer and lower competition: a cancer-risk umbrella review in Cancer Epidemiol (11-20), which answers the evergreen 'does Ozempic/Mounjaro cause cancer?' search with an RCT meta-analysis of 48 trials behind it; a SOUL repeat-events analysis for oral semaglutide (adults with T2D and CVD/CKD); and a 60-week semaglutide RCT on disordered-eating symptoms (needs careful handling). Search-demand formats requested in the playbook are included: pen how-to, Zepbound vial vs pen, what-to-expect at 6 months, the Foundayo label, Mounjaro vs Ozempic (SURPASS-2), hair loss, nausea and injection-site reactions. Rejected: compounded recalls (Greenwich Rx), compounded price lists, the kids' semaglutide NEJM trial and teen trials as long videos (wrong audience, growth fear-bait), NHS funding and Medicare negotiation (we avoid cost and access topics), retatrutide and implant pipeline items for Shorts, and black-market peptide seizures.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) not working, or slowing down? Why results vary from person to person: trial spread, metabolic adaptation ('energy-saving mode'), and why hunger can return while intake stays lower
candidates.angle: Answer first: in SURMOUNT-1 most people lost a lot, but the range was wide. Explain the three reasons the evidence supports (biology and genes, the body's metabolic adaptation, and real-world habits and adherence), then what tends to help: protein, strength training, and a talk with your prescriber. The news hook is the Ozempic 'stalls for some' study wave. The video is drug-first on tirzepatide and stays separate from our Plateau video by focusing on why people differ. Observational and review evidence is worded as 'may help explain'.
keywords: why weight loss varies on glp-1

candidates.why_now: The same story has moved from ScienceDaily (11-18) to SciTechDaily (11-21), Qazinform (11-22) and UNILAD (11-23). That is the jump from science outlets to mass media. It also builds on our earlier GLP1R gene-variant snapshot. January weight-loss searches peak about 5 weeks out.

evidence.signal: Metabolic adaptation may explain differing semaglutide responses; observational 6-month calorimetry study plus review

candidates.topic: Do Ozempic or Mounjaro cause cancer? What the newest umbrella review (Cancer Epidemiol, 20 Nov) and the RCT meta-analysis of 48 trials actually show, including the thyroid C-cell label warning
candidates.angle: A myth-check in a positive, reassuring tone. Across large meta-analyses of randomized trials, GLP-1 medicines and tirzepatide show little or no effect on obesity-related cancer risk. Some observational signals look lower for colorectal and liver cancer, but that is association only. Then explain clearly why the boxed thyroid warning (MTC or MEN 2) is still on the label. We never say it prevents cancer. Point out the J Clin Epidemiol 'laundered survival' critique of observational GLP-1 cancer-outcome studies as a reason for humility.
candidates.predicted_peak: 1–3 weeks (evergreen search; new review not yet in consumer press)
candidates.why_now: The umbrella review came out 11-20, and Targeted Onc and CancerNetwork ran 'GLP-1 and cancer prevention' pieces on 11-23. Consumer creators haven't covered it yet. 'Ozempic cancer' is a durable, high-volume search.

evidence.signal: Umbrella review of meta-analyses on GLP-1 RA cancer risk, 2026 Nov 20
48 RCTs, n=94,245: little or no effect on obesity-related cancer risk; consistent for semaglutide and tirzepatide

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide nausea: why it happens, when it usually eases, and what may help (plus the prebiotic-soda pilot RCT as a small supporting fact)
candidates.angle: A felt symptom answered in one sentence: slower stomach emptying, most common during dose escalation and easing over time per the label. Practical moves are smaller meals, stopping at fullness and avoiding greasy food. Present the pilot RCT honestly as small and early. Red flags (severe, persistent pain) go short and late.

candidates.topic: Wegovy pill and heart risk: the new SOUL analysis shows oral semaglutide cut first and repeat cardiovascular events (adults with T2D and heart disease and/or CKD)

The new angle is that repeat events fell too. Explain that SOUL used Rybelsus-type oral semaglutide in T2D, which is not the same as the obesity pill. Make this a chapter or Short pointing to the heart video.
